question: Does a timeout stop an opponent run?
answer: No. After a run of 8+ points, a timeout nets -0.31 points over the next 2:00 compared to playing on (CI -0.40 to -0.23).
findings: With a timeout, the next 2:00 nets +0.51 points (CI +0.44 to +0.58), n=9313.
With no timeout, the next 2:00 nets +0.83 points (CI +0.79 to +0.87), n=23790.
Both groups outscore the opponent after the run (mean reversion, plus they have the ball). The gap at the same state is -0.31.
In Q4 only, timeout minus none is -0.26 points (CI -0.42 to -0.10), n=6980.
method: The trigger is a score that makes an unanswered run of 8+ points, with at least 2:30 left in the quarter and the margin within 20. A timeout in that dead ball is compared to no timeout in the next 60 s, on net points over the next 120 s, matched on run size and quarter.
data: ESPN play-by-play via sportsdataverse, NBA 2011-12 to 2025-26, 16,242 games, 33,103 runs.
split_check: Timeout minus none was -0.32 points in 2012-19 (CI -0.44 to -0.22) and -0.31 in 2020-26 (CI -0.42 to -0.19).
